summary: One ordering rule for every durable writer of a document room: updates are stored in room commit order except that a live write's own updates sit right after the room state its fork was read at; every stored content_changed is measured against its stored prefix; a version is the fold through its doc_update_version and a write's version is the state at its own last update. Five windows on main break the spec's oracle (A: held browser updates stored after the write; B1: the version capture re-forks; B2: browser updates after the fork read measured without the write; C: settlement/snapshot/named versions over unstored updates; D: two browsers' updates stored out of observer order), plus multi-operation transactions; all are fixed.

tasks.work: storedorder.go checker (docs.CheckStoredOrder), its boundary unit test, the deterministic window tests (A x2, B1, B2 before commit, B2 commit-to-publish, C settlement, C snapshot, D two browsers, multi-operation accept, re-measured credit) and the soak with -stored-order-rounds; envoy-dispatch stored-order subcommand (--artifact, --since). This commit is main plus the tests: the failing-before proof.

documentUpdateClass seq + stored mark recorded in the drain loop (own class included); exact read point from the replica; flushThrough(tx, P) with credits landed inside commitConsuming (lock the room state for flushed classes; landed variant for a caller holding the lock); the worker runs flushThrough(own seq) and skips its own update when already stored (window D).

Live writes: lockDocumentRoom before the first fork read for every joined write (head read in the same statement), fork read once at P, flushThrough(P) before the first append, version from the frozen fork at the write's last update with in-flight credits bounded by the fork's credit sequence, refuseLostWrite on a scratch merge only when the room committed after P (windows A, B1, multi-operation).

Shadow: at commit the write's fork becomes the room's shadow (from P, until the drain reaches its last published update); provisional classes re-measured on the shadow by whoever stores them, in seq order; credits and settlement scheduling follow the stored class (true->false lands without an author, false->true credits the actor the room recorded); shadow freed when none provisional remain or the room fails; cold write whose room loads mid-write gets from = 0 (window B2).

Settlement, snapshot and named versions without a write take their read point, flushThrough(P), and record doc_update_version as the head after the flush; the settlement repair path flushes before its repair update and again at its versioned read point (window C).

docstest.DialContext without testing.TB (Dial wraps it); packages/envoy/loadtest/browsertype program: N peers per document, agent bearer + X-Dispatch-Actor session, typing / insert-and-delete / delete at a set rate into the documents the load step edits, prints updates sent per peer.

Existing tests whose expectations change (lostedit_test.go, mutation_test.go afterCaptureFork cases and TestSnapshotCreditsAnEditMadeBetweenItsAuthorsAndCopyOnTheNextVersion, settlement_repair_test.go, pending_authors_test.go, authors_test.go, settlement_credit_test.go), each named with its reason in the PR body, wording-only pins deleted; changelog fragment packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/INFRA-707-stored-order.yaml (kind Fixed); cmd/dispatch/README.md section for stored-order.

findings.finding: 1. Scope: the spec names window A only, but the oracle in acceptance 1/2 also fails on B1, B2, C, browser-browser reordering and multi-operation re-forks.
findings.answer: All are in scope (plan Design 1-9, tests per window); recorded as specDepartures[0] for the architect.

findings.finding: 2. The outcome's 'stored in the order its room committed them' cannot hold for updates the room commits between a write's fork read and its publish.
findings.answer: Rules 1-3 (write's updates right after its read point; classes against the stored prefix; versions are the fold at their doc_update_version); specDepartures[1].

findings.finding: 3. Versioning the write's own state reaches LEGION-269 (lost-write refusal), LEGION-479 (settlement keeps peer edits) and LEGION-503 (credit timing) tests.
findings.answer: Design 6 and 9 keep each behaviour (scratch-merge refusal; peer edits stored before the settlement version); the plan names the tests whose expectations change and requires each change explained in the PR body.

findings.finding: 4. Classes the server forces true and compacted rows differ from a fold by design; prefixes that do not render.
findings.answer: Rule 2 defines an unrenderable side as true; the checker has no exclusion list, does not check a compacted base row's own class, reports pending structs, and reports any forced class still off rule 2.

findings.finding: 5. Compaction folds history away; old history was written by main's code.
findings.answer: The checker reads live history while rooms are resident (cluster check runs before the browser peers disconnect), starts at the oldest retained row, reports checked/skipped counts with minimums, and --since folds rows older than the step as base without checking them.

findings.finding: 6. Acceptance 2 has no builder, no browser workload, no place to run; the renderer is unexported; docstest needs testing.TB; bearer sockets are sessions.
findings.answer: Built here: docs.CheckStoredOrder + envoy-dispatch stored-order, docstest.DialContext + loadtest/browsertype with agent bearer + X-Dispatch-Actor; proof run from INFRA-598's branch with --dispatch-commit at INFRA-707's head; replica count recorded; INFRA-598 wires it permanently (specDepartures[2]).

findings.finding: 7. Acceptance 3: noise undefined; harness has no browsers; lock-before-read may be untimed.
findings.answer: Rule fixed before head runs from docs/solutions/testing/a-gain-smaller-than-the-run-to-run-spread-...-pr2429.md (base spread, discard box_busy_before > 10%, base runs first); 1x step; edit and upload p50/p99; the browser-present cost is the soak's logged latency.

findings.finding: 8. Acceptance 1 needs deterministic red-on-main tests and a soak with a measured failure rate; round counting; CI budget.
findings.answer: Deterministic hook-driven tests per window plus a soak counting only rounds with an unstored browser update at the append; n >= max(3/p, 200); CI default small, recorded proof uses the flag.

findings.finding: 9. Acceptance 4 puts obligations on INFRA-605; #2445 already adds handed/stored marks.
findings.answer: Same mark, not a second; batch = flushThrough(max seq); the implementer sends the contract to INFRA-605's implementer; whichever merges second runs acceptance 1.

findings.finding: 10. Credits and settlement scheduling are decided at room time; a re-measured class moves them.
findings.answer: Design 8: credits and settlement scheduling follow the stored class; a test asserts the next version's authors and that a settlement ran.

findings.finding: 11. The spec's evidence (version equals render at N+2) fits windows A and B1 alike; the INFRA-643 oracle was never committed.
findings.answer: Each red test names its window; the checker is rewritten and committed.

specDepartures.spec: Outcome and acceptance name one case: an agent HTTP write landing on a warm room that already holds browser updates not yet stored.
specDepartures.plan: Also fixes browser updates committed after the write's fork read (version capture re-fork; their classes measured without the write), settlement, snapshot and named versions rendered over unstored updates, two browsers' updates stored out of commit order, transactions with several operations, and the credits and settlement scheduling a re-measured class moves.
specDepartures.evidence: Acceptance 1 and 2 check every version and every class. On main: captureLiveTextAndAuthors re-forks (mutation.go:1347-1367) while doc_update_version = max(version) (mutation.go:1516-1519); classes are measured against a replica without the write (websocket.go:526-544); settlement checks only hasPendingUpdates (service.go:1418-1425); consumeUpdateClass takes classes by bytes anywhere in the queue (roomstate.go:277-299).

outcome.scope: Adds windows B1, B2, C, two-browser reordering, multi-operation transactions and credit/settlement consequences to this issue.

specDepartures.spec: Dispatch stores a document's updates and versions in the order its room committed them.
specDepartures.plan: Updates are stored in room commit order except that a live write's own updates sit right after the room state its fork was read at; browser updates the room commits after that read are stored after the write, and every stored class is measured against its stored prefix.
specDepartures.evidence: The room receives a write only after its transaction commits (ledger.go:122-183, livewrite.go:652-769), while the write's version number is fixed at its append inside the transaction (persistence.go:203-265); updates the room commits between the read and the publish precede the write in the room but cannot precede it in the store.

summary: Dispatch stores a document's updates in the room's commit order, except that a live write's own updates follow the room state its fork was read at; every stored content_changed is measured against the state its stored prefix folds to, and every version is the fold through its doc_update_version.
